findings.governingReading: It was something that could not possibly happen: the room was locked from within.
findings.explanation: The English uses a stock dramatic phrase that weakens the narrator’s categorical impossibility.

findings.evidenceJa: 桜ちゃんが趣味で飾っていたギロチン
findings.governingReading: Sakura allegedly displayed the guillotine as a hobby.
findings.explanation: The English retains ornamentality but omits Sakura’s agency and the alleged hobby driving the joke.

findings.highlight: the instant someone got on it
findings.governingReading: The bed transforms into a guillotine the instant the victim lies down.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes an unspecified person getting onto it and weakens the staged mechanism.

findings.highlight: a direct offense brought on by an external factor
findings.evidenceJa: 外的要因による直接犯行
findings.governingReading: The second explanation is a direct crime committed through an external cause.
findings.explanation: The English’s “direct offense” is unnatural and obscures the murder-mystery category.

findings.evidenceJa: 壁に仕掛けてあった防犯機能・投げナイフ
findings.governingReading: The throwing-knife security device is installed in the wall.
findings.explanation: The English omits the wall placement needed for the locked-room gag’s physical explanation.

findings.evidenceJa: 二人の推理は過熱していく
findings.governingReading: The two detectives’ inferential reasoning grows increasingly heated.
findings.explanation: The English calls their deductions speculation, weakening the parody of formal detective reasoning.

findings.evidenceJa: 事件は一日前の午前中にさかのぼる
findings.governingReading: The case traces back to the previous morning.
findings.explanation: The English removes the case as subject and leaves a sentence fragment.

findings.governingReading: The detectives theatrically call the house a cursed mansion.
findings.explanation: The English changes a curse into haunting.

findings.highlight: I wish they’d never again do a one-time ridiculous Tiger Dojo
findings.evidenceJa: こういう一発芸は今回限りにしてほしい
findings.governingReading: The corpse asks that this kind of one-off stunt be limited to this occasion.
findings.explanation: The English makes the Tiger Dojo itself “one-time” and produces a contradictory request never to repeat something already defined as singular.
